paul_support: Heads-up — Acme reported repeated alert fires between 00:00–01:00 UTC last night. They say dashboards show no traffic but 'error_rate > 1%' alert triggered ~12x. Customer is unhappy, asking for root cause.
amelia: Which alert/rule id? any screenshots or rule config?
paul_support: Rule r-8042, metric alerts/error_rate_service_v2, threshold=1%, evaluation_window=5m, rollup=1m. Customer attached a screenshot showing flat 0% on the chart but many alert events.
monitor-bot: alert r-8042 fired 2027-06-15T00:12:05Z count=1
monitor-bot: alert r-8042 fired 2027-06-15T00:17:05Z count=1
amelia: Hmm. Could be aggregation buckets misaligned with the alert evaluation window. Devon — any recent rollup changes?
devon: Yep — we shipped a change to rollup-processor last week that altered how we compute bucket boundaries. If tz param is empty we accidentally use server local tz when building buckets.
devon: Example of the problematic code we traced:```sql
-- problematic rollup (uses server local time if params.tz is empty)
SELECT floor(extract(epoch from ts)/60)::int*60 AS bucket_ts_utc,
       count(*) AS errs
FROM events
WHERE service = 'api'
  AND ts >= '2027-06-15T00:00:00Z'
  AND ts <  '2027-06-15T01:00:00Z'
GROUP BY bucket_ts_utc;
```
devon: Logs from rollup-processor show lines like `bucket_start=2027-06-14T20:00:00-04:00 bucket_count=0` for many buckets — so 00:00 UTC got shifted into previous local day (EST) and produced empty buckets.
mike_sre: Confirmed on my end. Last deploy (2027-06-10) introduced a code path that calls `date_trunc('minute', ts AT TIME ZONE coalesce(params.tz, system_tz))`. system_tz on our canary hosts is America/New_York. That causes midnight-UTC windows to be split across wrong bucket boundaries.
amelia: Can you write concise repro steps so support can tell Acme?
devon: Repro steps: 1) Create rule with evaluation window aligned to UTC midnight (00:00 UTC). 2) Run rollup job on host with local tz != UTC and with params.tz unset. 3) Inspect buckets for 00:00–01:00 UTC — you'll see many 0-count buckets because they were assigned to previous local-day buckets. 4) Alerts that sum/avg across the window may hit threshold due to normalization over miscounted buckets.
mike_sre: Proposed mitigation: a) Hotfix rollup-processor to default to UTC when params.tz is null (simple patch), b) run a backfill re-aggregation for affected orgs for the last 48 hours, c) add unit/e2e tests for tz handling and add a lint rule to prevent implicit system_tz usage.
paul_support: ETA? Customer needs an ETA before escalation.
mike_sre: I have a patch ready. Will push to canary in 10m and verify. Backfill script is ready — estimate 1–2h for acme-corp dataset. If canary looks good we can promote to prod in the next maintenance window or faster if approved.
amelia: I'll tell Acme: temporary suppression of r-8042 for 3h while we patch + backfill, and we will follow up when resolved.
paul_support: Sounds good. Please post canary verification logs and tag me.
monitor-bot: deploy rollup-processor v2.3.7-canary started at 2027-06-15T01:05:00Z by devon
devon: Canary shows corrected bucket_start values now using UTC; example: `bucket_start=2027-06-15T00:00:00Z bucket_count=42`. No spurious empty buckets in the test dataset.
mike_sre: Kicked off backfill for acme-corp. Tracking id: backfill-8491. I'll post when complete.
amelia: Updated Acme and suppressed the alert. They appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
paul_support: Great work — please leave this thread with final resolution once backfill done.
mike_sre: Backfill complete for acme-corp at 2027-06-15T02:20:10Z. Verified charts show real counts and r-8042 no longer firing on historical windows. Patch rolled to prod and added tests.
amelia: Confirmed with customer, they closed the ticket. Thanks team.
